public_payload.normalized_proposition: Multiple studies have shown that most companies do not see a significant return on their AI investment.

statement.excerpt: None of this should be surprising; I have been pointing out the errors since the week ChatGPT was introduced in 2022, and study after study after study (I will go into this more in a later newsletter) has shown that most companies don’t seen a significant return on their AI investment.
statement.document_title: If enough other companies report the same, the bubble pops. 🫧

our_interpretation: The assessed proposition concerns published study findings, not the separate autobiographical statement about when Marcus began discussing errors.
Most means more than half. Significant means material realized business or financial benefit, not statistical significance.
The retrospective phrase 'has shown' covers studies available by May 26, 2026. No starting date for those studies is supplied.
Multiple independent studies can support the claim even if narrower studies find better results. Survey findings do not establish an audited return for every company.
criteria.support_condition: At least two studies available by the post date find that more than half of surveyed companies lack material realized benefits from AI investment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The purported supporting studies do not find a majority lacking material returns, or their relevant findings instead show a majority achieving such returns.

evidence.locator: Section 'AI emerges as a defining fault line for growth and profitability'
evidence.explanation: PwC's survey of 4,454 CEOs directly reports a majority without significant financial benefits. Fieldwork occurred from September through November 2025.
BCG's 2025 study reports another majority with little material value despite investment. This independently matches the ordinary meaning of the claim.

This study found positive median returns among finance functions and limited gains for about one-third. Its narrower population and different measurement do not overturn the two broader findings, but caution against claiming uniform results.
